start_here: Say to your AI: "Run workflow:keep-my-sidebar with store {\"where\": \"postgresql database example_me on my own computer\", \"language\": \"SQL (PostgreSQL)\", \"credential_name\": \"example-me-postgres-connection\"} and operations [{\"op\": \"change\", \"changes\": [{\"do\": \"make_list\", \"list_id\": \"waiting\", \"name\": \"Waiting on me\"}]}]."
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: the sidebar's lists, rows, rules and notes are kept in the person's own store, in whatever form that store keeps things, and store says where and in which language.
instructions: 1. Keep the store's login in your vault under a name you choose, and say where the store is and how it is spoken to.
2. Say "Run workflow:keep-my-sidebar" with store and, when you have them, the operations to run: changes, notes and a read.
3. The first run makes the store's own objects once and proves them on the example attempts: the prove step must give every expected outcome and the read-back, or the run stops and says which.
4. Every later run keeps the changes and notes in the limits (50 changes a batch, 280 characters a message, 4 screens offered) and reads the sidebar back.

worked_examples.title: A list made for my AIs and a note left on it
worked_examples.ask: Make a list called Waiting on me for the inbox screen, and leave the note 'Three things wait here.' on it.
worked_examples.given: The store holds no sidebar yet, and the look step found nothing.
worked_examples.hands_back: results ["kept", "kept"] and kept_records ["list:waiting", "row:screen:inbox", "note:1"], each read back in found_records; the sidebar then lists Waiting on me with one note.

store.where: postgresql database example_me on my own computer
